title: Rudolf Blaschka 1892 railway-clock audit
scope: Backend-only synchronization of Rudolf Blaschka's correspondence, postcard dates, railway timetables and the filmed Rakow sketchbook sequence for the Arizona-to-California phase of 22-26 April 1892.
frontend_policy: Do not alter public GitHub Pages in this pass. Sketchbook image-derived chronology, railway-clock refinements and route corrections remain research/backend only until explicitly approved.

source_hierarchy.rule: Rudolf's dated letters and cards control actual presence, reported arrival/departure times and retrospective descriptions of the immediately preceding journey.

source_hierarchy.class: same-year railway timetable or railroad publication
source_hierarchy.rule: Use to constrain plausible scheduled movement, but distinguish the publication/effective date from the exact day Rudolf travelled.
Use only as contextual control when the exact April 1892 issue is not yet recovered.
Use only to understand persistent route geometry or service pattern; never as proof of an 1892 train time.

time_standard_notes.historical_clock_guard: Do not silently normalize all historical times into a modern time-zone system. The Maricopa & Phoenix timetable explicitly labels its table 'Pacific time', while Rudolf notes that clocks had been set back several times during his transcontinental journey.
time_standard_notes.reported_times: Rudolf's 10 o'clock Los Angeles arrival, 8:45 Los Angeles departure, approximately 10 o'clock Pacific-Ocean sighting and 1 p.m. San Diego arrival are treated as the local railway/travel clock readings he reported, without modern UTC conversion.

chronology.event: Wagon excursion a few miles into the mountains and desert; cactus flowers drawn, living cactus examples collected, Delphinium drawn after return.
chronology.forward_plan: Rudolf says they will finish in Tempe the next day, go to Maricopa to spend the night, then take the Sunday-morning train to California.

chronology.basis: 22 April forward plan plus 24 April dated Maricopa cards/sketches.
chronology.event: Transfer to the Maricopa Southern Pacific junction and overnight stay.

chronology.evidence: BLA-D00786 · 017:140 and BLA-D00788 · 017:142; sketchbook pages 4-5 and 8-9
chronology.event: Rudolf is in Maricopa on Sunday 24 April. Two filmed sketchbook views are captioned Maricopa and dated 24 April. The strongest current interpretation is station-adjacent or rail-window landscape observation rather than a separate collecting excursion.

railway_clock_control.status: strong contextual control, not exact-day proof

Southern Pacific westbound passes Maricopa at 6:35 A.M.

railway_clock_control.guard: An issue-specific Southern Pacific timetable for 24 April 1892 has not yet been recovered, so 6:35 a.m. must remain contextual.

chronology.place: Maricopa → Yuma → California salt desert → Salton depression → San Jacinto approach
chronology.evidence: BLA-D00796–BLA-D00797 · 017:150–151, written 25 April and explicitly describing the preceding day's desert journey
chronology.status: secure corridor; internal segment timing unresolved
event_sequence: Arizona to Yuma: rocky mountain range behind chaparral, jumping cactus and giant cactus.
After crossing into California: sandy plain broadens and vegetation becomes sparse.
Approximately two hours through nearly vegetationless cracked sandy and rocky ground.
Railway after Yuma to Salton described as about 260 feet below sea level.
After the depression, railway climbs quickly toward roughly 2,000 feet.
Snow-covered San Jacinto is passed; vegetation shifts to large Yucca, blooming Opuntia and Abronia.

sketchbook_relation.assessment: The uncaptioned steep rocky desert massif is now best assigned to this 24 April rail-observation corridor rather than a generic 24-25 April interval.
sketchbook_relation.guard: Page sequence and letter chronology strengthen the date/corridor match but do not identify the mountain or precise milepoint.

chronology.evidence: BLA-D00797 · 017:151 plus Los Angeles postcard BLA-D00790 · 017:144 dated 25 April
chronology.event: Rudolf says they arrived in Los Angeles 'at 10' and had to stay overnight because the San Diego train did not leave until 8:45. Given the Sunday morning Maricopa departure, the long Arizona-California rail journey, overnight wording, and next-day San Diego arrival, 10 p.m. is overwhelmingly more plausible than 10 a.m.
Departure for San Diego at 8:45 after the Los Angeles overnight.

chronology.status: secure approximate time; exact coastal milepoint unresolved
chronology.event: Rudolf reports reaching/sighting the Pacific Ocean around 10 in the morning; from there the ocean remained in view toward San Diego.
chronology.route_context: The contemporary Southern California Railway/Santa Fe coastal alignment is consistent with a coastward transition south of Los Angeles, but an April 1892 timetable with station-by-station times remains to be recovered.

sketchbook_implications: Pages 4-5 and 8-9 are best treated as Maricopa transit-observation landscapes on 24 April, not evidence of a new formal collecting expedition.
Pages 12-13 can be dated more tightly to 24 April with high confidence because Rudolf's 25 April letter explicitly calls the Arizona-to-California desert sequence 'yesterday'.
The sketchbook therefore records observation made within transport windows as well as field excursions: railway carriage, station waiting and travel time function as observational infrastructure.

The next geolocation problem is no longer 'Arizona or California?' but which 24 April daylight segment — Arizona/Yuma, lower Colorado/California desert, Salton depression, or San Jacinto approach — best fits the p12/p13 silhouette.

railway_as_epistemic_infrastructure.working_claim: Railway time did not merely schedule movement between field sites. The timetable created windows in which landscapes could be observed, compared, sketched and retrospectively sequenced.
railway_as_epistemic_infrastructure.evidence_chain: dated card / timetable → moving visual sequence → sketchbook landscape → next-day letter reconstructing ecological succession
railway_as_epistemic_infrastructure.guard: Keep this as an interpretive synthesis grounded in the synchronized sources; do not claim that a particular sketch was physically drawn aboard the moving train unless additional evidence supports that action.

next_tests: Extract the station-by-station timetable panels from Southern Pacific January 1892 Rumsey item 3139B, especially Maricopa, Yuma, Salton/Indio and Los Angeles.
Locate the March-April 1892 Official Railway Guide and compare its Southern Pacific schedule with the 6:35 a.m. May control.
Recover an 1892 Southern California Railway / Santa Fe Los Angeles-San Diego timetable to test Rudolf's 8:45 departure, ~10 a.m. Pacific sighting and 1 p.m. San Diego arrival against station times.
Only after historical clock standards and station times are secured, calculate daylight windows for 24 April and eliminate p12/p13 mountain candidates that would have been passed in darkness.
Preserve the public map's present state until an explicit frontend correction pass is authorized.
